L4:   * ## 【2†Image: Company History】
L5: 
L6: * * *
L7: 
L8: 1889
L9: 
L10: Fusajiro Yamauchi began manufacturing and selling Japanese playing cards, Hanafuda, in Shimogyo-ku, Kyoto, Japan.
L11: 
L12: * * *
L13: 
L14: 1902
L15: 
L16: Started manufacturing and selling the first western playing cards in Japan.
L17: 
L18: * * *
L19: 
L20: 1947
L21: 
L22: Established Marufuku Co., Ltd., which is the previous incarnation of Nintendo Co., Ltd., in Higashikawara-cho, Imagumano, Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto, Japan.
L23: 
L24: * * *
L25: 
L26: 1951
L27: Changed the company's name to Nintendo Playing Card Co., Ltd.
L28: 
L29: * * *
L30: 
L31: 1952
L32: 
L33: Consolidated the manufacturing facilities, which used to be scattered around Kyoto, in Kamitakamatsu-cho, Fukuine, Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto, Japan.
L34: 
L35: * * *
L36: 
L37: 1953
L38: 
L39: Became the first company to succeed in mass-producing plastic playing cards in Japan.
L40: 
L41: * * *
L42: 
L43: 1959
L44: 
L45: Moved the headquarters to Kamitakamatsu-cho, Fukuine, Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto, Japan.
L46: Started selling Disney character playing cards.
L47: 
L48: * * *
L49: 
L50: 1961
L51: Established the Tokyo Branch in Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo, Japan.
L52: 
L53: * * *
L54: 
L55: 1962
L56: 
L57: Listed stock on the Second Section of the Osaka Securities Exchange and on the Kyoto Stock Exchange.
L58: 
L59: * * *
L60: 
L61: 1963
L62: 
L63: Changed the company's name to Nintendo Co., Ltd. (current name).
L64: 
L65: * * *
L66: 
L67: 1968
L68: 
L69: Automated the production of Japanese playing cards with machines that paste backing paper onto the cards.
L70: 
L71: * * *
L72: 
L73: 1970
L74: 
L75: Stock listing was changed to the First Section of the Osaka Securities Exchange.
L76: 
L77: * * *
L78: 
L79: 1973
L80: Developed an entertainment system called Laser Clay Shooting System for leisure facilities.
L81: 
L82: * * *
L83: 
L84: 1977
L85: 
L86: Launched Nintendo's first home video game machines, TV Game 15 and TV Game 6.
L87: 
L88: * * *
L89: 
L90: 1978
L91: 
L92: Developed and started selling arcade video game machines.
L93: 
L94: * * *
L95: 
L96: 1980
L97: 
L98: Developed and started selling GAME & WATCH.
L99: Established a wholly-owned subsidiary, Nintendo of America Inc., in New York, U.S.A.
L100: 
L101: * * *
L102: 
L103: 1981
L104: 
L105: Developed and started selling an arcade video game called Donkey Kong.
L106: 
L107: * * *
L108: 
L109: 1982
L110: Established Nintendo of America Inc. in Seattle, Washington and merged the New York subsidiary into it.
L111: 
L112: * * *
L113: 
L114: 1983
L115: 
L116: Listed stock on the First Section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
L117: Launched the home video game system, Family Computer System (known as Nintendo Entertainment System outside Japan.)
L118: Established a new manufacturing plant, which is now Uji Plant, in Uji City, Kyoto.
L119: 
L120: * * *
L121: 
L122: 1985
L123: 
L124: Started selling the Super Mario Bros. game software for the Nintendo Entertainment System.
L125: 
L126: * * *
L127: 
L128: 1989
L129: Launched the handheld video game system, Game Boy.
L130: 
L131: * * *
L132: 
L133: 1990
L134: 
L135: Launched the home video game system, Super Famicom (known as Super Nintendo Entertainment System outside Japan.)
L136: Established Nintendo of Europe GmbH (currently Nintendo of Europe SE) in Germany.
L137: 
L138: * * *
L139: 
L140: 1996
L141: 
L142: Launched the home video game system, Nintendo 64.
L143: 
L144: * * *
L145: 
L146: 2000
L147: 
L148: The headquarters of Nintendo Co., Ltd. was relocated to 11-1 Hokotate-cho, Kamitoba, Minami-ku, Kyoto, Japan (current location).
L149: 
L150: * * *
L151: 
L152: 2001
L153: Launched the handheld video game system, Game Boy Advance. Launched the home video game system, Nintendo GameCube.
L154: 
L155: * * *
L156: 
L157: 2004
L158: 
L159: Launched the handheld video game system, Nintendo DS.
L160: 
L161: * * *
L162: 
L163: 2006
L164: 
L165: Launched the home video game system, Wii.
L166: 
L167: * * *
L168: 
L169: 2008
L170: 
L171: Launched the handheld video game system, Nintendo DSi.
L172: 
L173: * * *
L174: 
L175: 2011
L176: 
L177: Launched the handheld video game system, Nintendo 3DS.
L178: 
L179: * * *
L180: 
L181: 2012
L182: 
L183: Launched the home video game system, Wii U.
L184: 
L185: * * *
L186: 
L187: 2014
L188: 
L189: Launched the handheld video game system, New Nintendo 3DS.
L190: * * *
L191: 
L192: 2016
L193: 
L194: Released smart device application, Miitomo.
L195: 
L196: * * *
L197: 
L198: 2017
L199: 
L200: Launched Nintendo Switch, a home video game system that can also be used as a handheld.
L201: Established Nintendo Sales Co., Ltd. in Taito-ku, Tokyo.
L202: 
L203: * * *
L204: 
L205: 2018
L206: 
L207: Started the online service, Nintendo Switch Online.
L208: 
L209: * * *
L210: 
L211: 2019
L212: 
L213: Opened Japan's first official flagship store, Nintendo TOKYO, in Shibuya, Tokyo.
L214: 
L215: * * *
L216: 
L217: 2021
L218: 
L219: The world’s first Nintendo theme park land, SUPER NINTENDO WORLD, opened at Universal Studios Japan.
L220: 
L221: * * *
L222: 
L223: 2022
L224: Nintendo Co., Ltd. transitioned to the Prime Market of the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
L225: 
L226: * * *
L227: 
L228: 2023
L229: 
L230: Release of The Super Mario Bros. Movie, the first animated movie produced in partnership with Nintendo.
L231: 
L232: * * *
L233: 
L234: 2024
L235: 
L236: Nintendo's public relations facility, the Nintendo Museum, opened in Uji-shi Kyoto. Here, visitors can discover the history of the entertainment that Nintendo has been offering and experience its entertainment.
L237: 
L238: * * *
L239: 
L240: 2025
L241: 
L242: Launched the home video game system, Nintendo Switch 2.
L243: 
L244: * * *

L180: (as of May 19, 2026)
L181: 
L182: Capcom is a game software developer based in Osaka. We have grown steadily over the years by using our expertise in developing highly-original games and then leveraging this content across various mediums through our Single Content Multiple Usage strategy.

L215: ## Origin of “Capcom” Name
L216: 
L217: CAPCOM was founded in 1983, when game machines became widely acknowledged as a popular entertainment medium from a niche market.
L218: 
L219: This trend was a major motivating factor as CAPCOM was founded to create content based on a new kind of entertainment: “people matching wits against computers”.
L220: 
L221: 【79†Image: CAPCOM logo】
L222: The name CAPCOM is an abbreviation of CAPsule COMputer. This was a phrase symbolic of an internal company objective to create a new gaming experience that would exceed that of rival personal computers which had also been increasing in popularity during the same period.
L223: 
L224: The “Capsule” segment of the CAPCOM name was based on 2 key concepts: “a container packed to the brim with fun” and “a desire to create securely packaged games to decrease the rapid expansion of pirated materials”.

L4: # Basic Information about KONAMI
L5: 
L6: Updated date June 25, 2026
L7: 
L8: ### History of KONAMI
L9: 
L10: #### When was KONAMI founded?
L11: 
L12: KONAMI was founded in March 1969 as a jukebox retail and repair business in Toyonaka City, Osaka, Japan by Kagemasa Kozuki, the still-current Director, Chairman.
L13: 
L14: #### When was KONAMI established?
L15: 
L16: KONAMI was established as Konami Industries Co., Ltd. (currently KONAMI GROUP CORPORATION) in March 1973.
L17: #### When was the initial listing of KONAMI shares on the stock exchange?
L18: 
L19: It was first listed on the second section of the Osaka Securities Exchange in October 1984.
L20: 
L21: #### On what stock exchanges is KONAMI currently listed?
L22: 
L23: KONAMI is listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange and the London Stock Exchange.
L24: #### When was KONAMI shares listed on the first section (current "Prime Market") of the Tokyo Stock Exchange?
L25: 
L26: It was listed in August 1988. In April 2022, KONAMI transitioned its listing to the "Prime Market" of the Tokyo Stock Exchange upon its market segment restructure.
L27: 
L28: #### When was KONAMI listed on the London Stock Exchange?
L29: 
L30: It was listed in September 1999.
L31: 
L32: ### Stock, Dividend and Returns
L33: 
L34: #### What is the security code of KONAMI?
L35: 
L36: The security code is 9766 (Tokyo Stock Exchange).
L37: #### What is the ticker symbol used on the London Stock Exchange?
L38: 
L39: The ticker symbol is KNM.
L40: 
L41: #### What is the number of issued shares?
L42: 
L43: As of March 31, 2026, the number of issued shares is 143,500,000 (including 7,943,517 shares of treasury stock).
L44: #### How do I contact KONAMI's transfer agent?
L45: 
L46: Our transfer agent is Sumitomo Mitsui Trust Bank, Limited. They can help with a variety of shareholder-related services. The contact details are as follows:
L47: 
L48: Sumitomo Mitsui Trust Bank, Limited
L49: Stock Transfer Agency Department
L50: 2-8-4 Izumi, Suginami-ku, Tokyo 168-0063, Japan
L51: Toll Free: 0120-782-031(available within Japan)
L52: Web site: 【2†https://www.smtb.jp/personal/procedure/agency†www.smtb.jp】 (in Japanese)
L53: #### When is the dividend record date?
L54: 
L55: Year-end cash dividends are at the end of March and interim dividends are at the end of September each year.
L56: 
L57: #### How much was KONAMI's most recent annual dividend?
L58: 
L59: Our annual dividend for FY2026 was 221.50yen per share.

L73: ### Financials
L74: 
L75: #### When is KONAMI's fiscal year end?
L76: 
L77: It is on March 31.
